clue.text: A spirited community? Anything but!

parts.note: a settlement full of spirits in the spooky sense, yet utterly lifeless and deserted rather than lively

explanation.surface: A sardonic remark about a dull village that is anything but lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' seems to mean lively, and the place is the opposite of lively; but it is also literally haunted, home only to spectres.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned settlement whose inhabitants have all left is said to be haunted, peopled only by phantoms.

clue.text: Bachelor has to proceed by degrees

definitions.meaning: someone holding a bachelor's degree from a university
to move forward step by step

explanation.surface: An unmarried man is advised to take things slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a first university degree, and a verb meaning to advance gradually in stages.

clue.text: Utterly direct

explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means completely; as an adjective, plain and unqualified, as in a blunt refusal.

clue.text: Cretan wandered round in a daze

indicators.note: the letters of the island-dweller's word roam about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man from Crete walked about in a stupor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandered round' rearranges CRETAN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotic, dreamlike state of semi-consciousness is a stupor or daze.

clue.text: Not the in-crowd, for a start

parts.note: the opposite of in is out
a set is a group or circle of people

explanation.surface: Those who are unfashionable are listed first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in-crowd' reads as one fashionable clique, but the hyphenated word splits between the two pieces; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, as in 'from the very beginning'.

clue.text: Secure folder used by a manicurist

parts.note: to nail is to fasten firmly
a file is a folder for papers

explanation.surface: A locked document wallet belongs to a beauty technician.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the description 'used by a manicurist', standing for the implement itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A small abrasive tool for shaping fingertips is standard equipment for a hand-care specialist.

clue.text: Fur acquired from sale in Belgium

indicators.note: the country's code letter is placed inside the word sale

parts.note: taken as written
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A fur coat was bought at a market in Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelt of a small dark-furred marten prized in the fur trade.

clue.text: Stay the night to finish cricket match

parts.note: to stop is to finish
an over is a set of six balls bowled in a cricket match

explanation.surface: A player stays overnight to complete a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is the basic unit of bowling in cricket, six deliveries from one end; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To break a journey and lodge somewhere overnight before travelling on.

clue.text: A fat ram, for instance

definitions.meaning: a dairy fat spread on bread
a male sheep, an example of an animal that butts with its head

explanation.surface: A plump male sheep, say.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: one who butts, as a ram does.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy spread churned from cream; also, playfully, any creature that butts with its horns.

clue.text: Six points made by ascetic Jew

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
S is south, a compass point
S is south again
E is east again
N is north, a compass point
E is east a third time

explanation.surface: A religious hermit scores six points in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six points' gives six single compass letters; 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Member of an austere Jewish sect of the Second Temple period, linked to the Dead Sea Scrolls.

clue.text: Lure army reservists back to open ground

indicators.note: the reservists' abbreviation is turned around, read from the end

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: An instruction to entice reserve soldiers back onto open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TA into AT; the Territorial Army is Britain's part-time reserve force. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice or draw something in, as bait does fish.

clue.text: Jack and Peter produced a preservative

parts.note: a jack and a salt are both slang for a sailor

indicators.note: the name is worked up into a fresh arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Two men jointly came up with a way of keeping food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges PETER into PETRE; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, used for curing meat and in gunpowder, a classic food preservative.

clue.text: A university chap accommodates many by offering increase

indicators.note: the word for a man houses the letter for many within it

parts.note: a gent is a chap
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many

explanation.surface: A college man takes in lots of people to grow numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodates' puts M inside GENT; 'by offering' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make greater or larger; to enlarge or boost.

clue.text: Anything but prosaic?

parts.note: the reverse of prose is poetry, so written in rhyme and metre rather than plain sentences

explanation.surface: A question about something thrillingly unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prosaic' seems to mean dull; read literally it means in prose. Split as two words the answer means 'in poetry', and as one it means opposite, which 'Anything but' also hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Written as poetry is the opposite of written in prose; as one word it also means contrary.

clue.text: Grieve to have restaurant meal without the beloved

indicators.note: here means outside: the dining phrase surrounds the term of endearment

parts.note: to eat out is to dine at a restaurant
one's heart is one's sweetheart, the one loved

explanation.surface: A jilted lover consoles themself by dining out alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the dining phrase wraps the term of endearment; 'to have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine or suffer in silent sorrow, longing for what one cannot have.

clue.text: Swimming race held without a team leader

indicators.note: the people-word is kept outside, wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: a nation is a people or race

indicators.note: the leader of team is its first letter

explanation.surface: A swimming event goes ahead with no team captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held without' puts A and T (team's 'leader') inside NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal term for the act or sport of moving through water by strokes.

clue.text: Explain precisely why coppers are involved in betrayal

indicators.note: the coins are tucked inside the word for treachery

parts.note: a sell-out is a betrayal
P stands for pence, copper coins

explanation.surface: Asking why police officers took part in a treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police but means pennies, P. 'are involved in' puts P inside SELLOUT; 'why' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out in full detail, letter by letter, leaving nothing unclear.

clue.text: Failure to feature appeal by embassy

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: An appeal from a consulate has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving something out, so that it does not appear or is not included.

clue.text: It makes the motorist put his foot down

definitions.text: It makes the motorist put his foot down

parts.words: It makes the motorist put his foot down
parts.note: the pedal pressed to speed up, rather than a driver taking a firm stand

explanation.surface: Something that makes a driver insist on getting their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put his foot down' sounds like taking a firm line, but literally means pressing the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: The valve controlling fuel to an engine, worked by the accelerator pedal.

clue.text: Chatter quietly and chatter on

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
to rattle on is to chatter at length

explanation.surface: Talking softly and then talking some more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish, inconsequential talk; babble.

clue.text: Nit-picker gets judo expert in a huff

indicators.note: the martial-arts grade goes inside the word for a sulk

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
a dan is a black-belt grade in judo

explanation.surface: A fussy person gets cross with a martial artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excessively fussy about minor details and rules.

clue.text: A loose woman in the family

parts.note: to loose is to untie, set free

explanation.surface: A promiscuous female relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective about morals; it is the verb meaning to unfasten.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister, a female relative, familiarly.

clue.text: Withdraw commission from money-handler

definitions.meaning: to dismiss an officer from the armed forces in disgrace
a bank or shop employee who takes and pays out cash

explanation.surface: Take away a bank clerk's commission.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing an officer from service in disgrace; also the person at a till or bank counter who deals with cash.

clue.text: Church requires examination of its music

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A church insists that its music be tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the church, so the definition is music sung by a church choir; 'requires' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for music sung by a choir, as heard in a church.

clue.text: One who drinks with a meal

definitions.meaning: someone who sups, taking liquid in sips

explanation.surface: A drinker accompanied by food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Playfully, someone who sips; also the last meal of the day.

clue.text: Spanish title given to a count and old sculptor

parts.note: Don is a Spanish honorific for a gentleman
to tell is to count, as in telling beads

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman is made a count and an elderly artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman to go with 'Spanish title' but is the verb TELL; 'given to' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Florentine Renaissance artist famous for his bronze David.

clue.text: Agent isn't meaning to decorate again

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: An agent says they don't intend to redecorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meaning' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a fresh coat of colour is redecorating.

clue.text: Association that is in the money

indicators.note: the Latin abbreviation is set inside the slang word for cash

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A partnership that is making a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the money' reads as prosperous; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A connection or link between things, such as a product linked to a film.

clue.text: Patience gets no treacle pudding

indicators.note: the letters are mixed together like a pudding's ingredients

explanation.surface: A tolerant person is denied a syrup dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' rearranges NO TREACLE; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance; the ability to put up with things without complaint.
